page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E6.Ax.Flex.1-8 is an entry-tier general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 9J45 processor running at a base clock speed of 2.7 GHz. The instance configuration allocates 1 dedicated physical core providing 2 virtual CPUs via simultaneous multithreading, paired with 8.0 GB of system memory to maintain a standard 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU.

Hardware resources on this instance do not include integrated local disk storage, which necessitates the attachment of external block volumes for root filesystems and persistent application data. There are no GPU accelerators present on the system. Network capabilities include one complimentary public IPv4 address for outbound and inbound connectivity.

Given its dedicated CPU thread allocation and balanced resource distribution, VM.Standard.E6.Ax.Flex.1-8 provides predictable compute for entry-level operations. It is technically appropriate for lightweight web serving, containerized microservices, development or test environments, continuous integration agents, and small background utility services.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E6.Ax.Flex.1-8 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture. Driven by an AMD EPYC 9J45 processor clocked at 2.7 GHz, the instance provides 1 physical core configured as 2 dedicated vCPUs with 2 threads per core. System memory is set at 8.0 GB, yielding a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per virtual core. The instance includes no integrated local storage or hardware accelerators, requiring external block storage for persistent data management. One complimentary public IPv4 address is included for network interfacing. Due to its dedicated CPU execution and compact resource footprint, VM.Standard.E6.Ax.Flex.1-8 is well suited for baseline enterprise tasks, including microservice execution, staging and development environments, low-traffic web serving, CI/CD worker nodes, and background job processing.
